questions.q: Seven people, B, C, D, I, J, K and L, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. L sits third to the left of I. Only one person sits between K and B when counted from the left of B. C sits third to the right of D. C sits to the immediate right of L. J is not an immediate neighbour of L. How many people sit between J and B when counted from the right of J?
questions.solution:
Use left as clockwise and right as anticlockwise for people facing the centre. The L–I spacing, C next to L, and D–C spacing fix most positions. Completing K, B and J leaves three people between J and B from J’s right.
**Answer: Three**

questions.q: In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic. FOUR - ORUF - RUOF TENS - ESNT - SNET
questions.solution:
The second group takes letters in order 2, 4, 3, 1, and the third reverses the original word. PLUG becomes LGUP and GULP, matching the given pattern.
**Answer: PLUG - LGUP - GULP**

questions.q: Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only. (Left) 1 3 5 2 7 1 9 5 1 7 8 4 2 5 7 6 6 5 3 4 7 2 1 7 7 4 9 (Right) How many such odd numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
questions.solution:
Scan three adjacent numbers at a time, looking for odd–odd–even. The qualifying centres are at positions 3, 10, 15, 19 and 25, giving five.
**Answer: Five**

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (18, 15.7, 19.2) (24, 21.7, 25.2)
questions.solution:
Subtract 2.3 from the first number and add 3.5 to the second. The matching set is 31 → 28.7 → 32.2.
**Answer: (31, 28.7, 32.2)**

questions.q: In a row of people all facing north, Aftab is 18 th from the right end. Apoorva is 28 th from the right end. Apoorva is exactly between Aftab and Piyali. If Piyali is 12 th from the left end of the line, how many people are there in the row?
questions.solution:
Apoorwa is ten places to the left of Aftab. As the midpoint, she is also ten places right of Piyali, making Piyali 38th from the right. Total = 38 + 12 - 1 = 49.
**Answer: 49**

questions.q: Refer to the following number, symbol series and answer the question. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers. (Left) % € € % 6 £ 3 & 1 £ 4 5 7 2 2 & & 9 & 8 8 * (Right) How many such symbols are there each of which is immediately preceded by a number and also immediately followed by a number?
questions.solution:
The symbols between two numbers are £ between 6 and 3, & between 3 and 1, £ between 1 and 4, and & between 9 and 8. Count = 4.
**Answer: 4**

questions.q: If + means - , - means x , x means ÷ , ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 15 – 10 ÷ 4 + 20 x 5 = ?
questions.solution:
Replace the signs: 15 × 10 + 4 - 20/5. Multiplication and division first give 150 + 4 - 4 = 150.
**Answer: 150**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘VAIL’ is coded as ‘6598’ and ‘OVAL’ is coded as ‘8619’. What is the code for ‘O’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
V, A and L occur in both words and share codes 6, 9 and 8. The extra letter O corresponds to the extra digit 1.
**Answer: 1**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 99 87 75 63 51 ?
questions.solution:
The sequence decreases by 12 each time. Next term = 51 - 12 = 39.
**Answer: 39**

questions.q: Mayank starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards the East. He then takes a left turn, drives 6 km, turns left and drives 17 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 15 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified).
questions.solution:
Horizontal travel cancels: 9 - 17 + 8 = 0. Vertical travel leaves him 9 km south of A. He must drive 9 km north to return.
**Answer: 9 km to the North**

questions.q: In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic. BLUE - LBUE - ELBU TWIN - WTIN - NWTI
questions.solution:
Swap the first two letters, then move the final letter to the front. FOUR becomes OFUR, then ROFU.
**Answer: FOUR - OFUR - ROFU**

questions.q: Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). (Counting to be done from left to right only.) (Left) 1 9 6 4 8 8 9 8 7 7 6 5 8 3 4 3 7 5 9 1 5 2 7 1 1 5 9 (Right) How many such even numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
questions.solution:
Check every interior even number for odd neighbours on both sides. The five qualifying centres are at positions 8, 11, 13, 15 and 22.
**Answer: 5**

questions.q: A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. R sits to the immediate left of U. B sits to the immediate left of C. C sits second to the left of T. A sits third to the left of U. Who sits third to the right of S?
questions.solution:
Fix U, then place R one position left and A three left. The T–C–B constraints fill the remaining places and S takes the final gap. A sits third to S’s right.
**Answer: A**

questions.q: A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. A sits fourth to the left of Y. W sits fourth to the right of C. Only two people sit between Y and C when counted from the left of Y. X is not an immediate neighbour of W or Y. D is not an immediate neighbour of X. Who sits third to the right of B?
questions.solution:
Place C three left of Y, A four left of Y, and W four right of C. The restrictions on X and D fix the remaining seats. D is third to B’s right.
**Answer: D**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.solution:
The common shifts are -2 for the first letter and -3 for the second. GK → EI uses -2 for both, making it the different pair.
**Answer: GK-EI**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 8 18 30 44 ? 78
questions.solution:
The differences are +10, +12, +14, +16 and +18. The missing number is 44 + 16 = 60.
**Answer: 60**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.solution:
Three pairs shift the first letter back three and the second back two. JM → GL shifts the second back only one, so it is the odd pair.
**Answer: JM-GL**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pathways are roads. No pathway is a garden. Conclusions: (I): Some gardens are roads. (II): All roads are gardens.
questions.solution:
Roads outside the pathway group may or may not be gardens, so some gardens being roads is not guaranteed. Roads containing the excluded pathways also cannot all be gardens. Neither conclusion follows.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows**

questions.q: In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic. GIFT - IFGT - TFIG LAND - ANLD - DNAL
questions.solution:
The second cluster takes positions 2, 3, 1, 4, and the third reverses the original. FLAG gives LAFG and GALF.
**Answer: FLAG - LAFG - GALF**

questions.q: Mr. Zzz starts from Point A and drives 8 km towards east. He then takes a right turn, drives 11 km, turns right and drives 17 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 21 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 9 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
questions.solution:
East–west movement cancels: 8 - 17 + 9 = 0. North–south movement gives -11 + 21 = 10 km north. He must travel 10 km south to reach A.
**Answer: 10 km to the south**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? MEW154, SKC131, YQI108, EWO85, ?
questions.solution:
Each letter advances six places, wrapping around the alphabet. Numbers decrease by 23. EWO85 is followed by KCU62.
**Answer: KCU62**

questions.q: In a certain code language, P @ Q means ‘P is the husband of Q’, P # Q means ‘P is the brother of Q’, P & Q means ‘P is the mother of Q’, and P % Q means ‘P is the sister of Q’. Based on the above, how is D related to E if ‘D # S @ Z & M % E’?
questions.solution:
S is Z’s husband, Z is M’s mother, and M is E’s sister. Thus S is E’s father. D is S’s brother, so D is E’s paternal uncle.
**Answer: Father's brother**

questions.q: If each of the digits in the number 243178569 is arranged in descending order from left to right, then what will be the sum of the digits which are second from the right and third from the left in the new number thus formed?
questions.solution:
The descending order is 987654321. Second from the right is 2 and third from the left is 7. Sum = 9.
**Answer: 9**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? QIS38, SLQ42, UOO46, ?
questions.solution:
The three letter columns move by +2, +3 and -2, respectively; the number increases by four. After UOO46 comes WRM50.
**Answer: WRM50**

questions.q: Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below S. Only one box is kept above Q. Only one box is kept between Q and P. R is kept immediately above N. O is kept at some place below M. How many boxes are kept between M and R?
questions.solution:
The order from top is M, Q, O, P, S, R, N. Q, O, P and S lie between M and R, giving four boxes.
**Answer: Four**

questions.q: If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 113 − 9 ÷ 17 + 519 × 3 = ?

Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers. (Left) # € % # 6 & 4 * 9 6 @ 5 % @ # © 8 # % * £ 2 (Right) How many such numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.solution:
The qualifying numbers are 6 between # and &, 4 between & and *, 5 between @ and %, and 8 between © and #. Count = 4.
**Answer: 4**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 621 623 627 633 641 ?
questions.solution:
Add successive even numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8 and then 10. Next term = 641 + 10 = 651.
**Answer: 651**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some cars are vehicles. All vehicles are machines. Conclusions (I): Some machines are cars. (II): No cars are machines.
questions.solution:
Some cars are vehicles, and all vehicles are machines. Those cars must be machines, so some machines are cars. Conclusion I follows and conclusion II is contradicted.
**Answer: Only conclusion (I) follows**
